sections.h2: Who sends and who values in Martin County?
sections.html:
The Martin County Property Appraiser values property, and the Martin County Tax Collector sends bills and collects them. Both offices are county constitutional offices, and the clerk's Official Records hold recorded deeds and liens.

  • Martin County Property Appraiser: real property parcel search by parcel ID, account number, subdivision, address or owner last name, plus published millage and census-based county statistics.
  • Martin County Tax Collector: tax statements, alternative payment plans, delinquent taxes and certificates, an important-dates page, a tangible personal property page and a glossary. Offices operate in Stuart, Hobe Sound, Indiantown and Palm City, and the phone line is 772-288-5600.
  • Martin County Clerk Official Records: the search for recorded instruments.

Call the collector about amounts owed and the appraiser about value, exemptions and parcel records.

sections.h2: What does the Martin County Property Appraiser report about the county?
sections.html:
The appraiser's home page says ten taxing authorities levy property taxes against Martin County parcels, and each proposes its own millage rate before public hearings adopt the budgets. Commercial and industrial parcels are 3.6% of real property parcels, per the appraiser.

The same page lists the headings it tracks: total market value, land area in square miles, single family homes, condo units, parks and natural areas, golf courses, restaurants, population, median household income, owner-occupied housing, population per square mile, housing units and veterans, with the data sourced from census.gov. Open the page to see the current values, since they change with each year's roll.

The page also notes that a proposed constitutional amendment on Florida property taxes was on the November 2026 general election ballot, and that approval by at least 60% of voters would put changes into effect January 1, 2027. Check the appraiser's site for what followed.

sections.h2: Where do Martin County residents pay and find help?
sections.html:
The tax collector runs four offices: Stuart, Hobe Sound, Indiantown and Palm City. The home page shows estimated wait times and people waiting at each office, and the office says e-checks are free. Its online payment pages and the county-taxes portal let owners look up accounts without a visit.

The same website carries a glossary of tax terms, a page on tangible personal property taxes, a frequently asked questions page on tax certificate sales and a page on alternative payment plans. Because the collector warns that site information is not guaranteed for legal purposes and may change daily, confirm any amount by phone before you rely on it for a closing.

Owners who want to understand the value side go to the property appraiser's parcel search and can compare their TRIM notice against the published roll data. A buyer's lender or title company will often ask for both the appraiser record and the collector's account history.

sections.h2: When are Martin County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Martin County tax statements are normally mailed on or about November 1, and the gross amount is due by March 31. Discounts run from 4% in November down to 1% in February.

Martin County Tax Collector calendar, as printed on its Important Tax Dates page
MonthWhat the collector lists
NovemberCollection begins, 4% discount through November 30
December3% discount; third installment due by December 31 with 3% discount
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchGross amount due by March 31; fourth installment due

SeptemberSecond installment due by September 30 with 4.5% discount

sections.h2: What does delinquency cost in Martin County?
sections.html:
On April 1 the collector adds 3% interest to unpaid real property taxes. Unpaid business personal property accrues 1.5% per month plus a $2.00 delinquent fee, and those accounts are advertised in a local newspaper within 45 days.

For real estate, the collector's calendar describes a newspaper ad run weekly over three weeks before the certificate sale, with the ad cost charged to the delinquent parcel. A certificate holder must wait two years before contacting the owner for payment, and a tax deed application can follow after that.

sections.h2: Is there an installment plan in Martin County?
sections.html:
Yes. The collector offers an alternative payment plan with four payments. State law gives the program as section 197.222, with the application due by April 30 per the Martin collector's calendar for the next year.

  • June 30: first payment with a 6% discount.
  • July: a late first payment may be accepted with a 5% penalty, otherwise participation is canceled.
  • September 30: second payment with a 4.5% discount.
  • December 31: third payment with a 3% discount.
  • March 31: fourth and final payment.

Enrolled taxpayers do not need to reapply to continue the program. A seller who is partway through the plan should ask the collector what is left, since the remaining portion is settled when the sale closes.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can lower a Martin County bill?
sections.html:
Martin County owners file with the property appraiser, and the first deadline falls in early March.

  • Homestead takes up to $50,000 off value. School taxes see only the first $25,000 of it.
  • A state cap limits yearly growth on a homestead. The state's chart prints 2.7% for 2026.
  • Other property has a 10 percent annual ceiling.
  • Portability carries cap savings to a new homestead, for up to $500,000 of difference. The statute page notes that chapter 2026-239 changes first apply to the 2027 roll.
  • A service-connected disability of 10 percent or more earns a $5,000 reduction in assessed value for an honorably discharged Florida resident.

A sale resets the parcel to market-based value the following January. The TRIM notice arrives in August and petitions go to the clerk.

sections.h2: How does Martin County tax get settled at a sale?
sections.html:
The collector's payoff number lets the title company clear the tax when the sale funds. The collector's offices in Stuart, Hobe Sound, Indiantown and Palm City can all be reached at 772-288-5600 about whether a certificate exists.

Florida charges deed stamp tax at 70 cents per $100 of consideration. A contract-for-deed buyer on record is among those notified before a tax deed sale, so a land contract does not hide a parcel from the process.

faqs.q: When are Martin County property tax statements mailed?
faqs.a: On or about November 1 each year, according to the Martin County Tax Collector. The gross amount is due by March 31.

faqs.q: What interest does Martin County add after April 1?
faqs.a: The collector's calendar lists a 3% interest charge on unpaid real property taxes. Tangible personal property accrues 1.5% per month plus a $2.00 fee.

faqs.q: Does Martin County have an installment plan for property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. It has four payments due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, with discounts of 6%, 4.5% and 3% on the first three. Applications are due by April 30.

faqs.q: Who do I call in Martin County about my tax account?
faqs.a: Call the Martin County Tax Collector at 772-288-5600. For parcel values and exemptions, contact the Martin County Property Appraiser.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Martin County house if taxes are overdue?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance can be cleared through closing. Get the payoff and any certificate details from the collector beforehand.
